en: Dr. Fe del Mundo invented a bamboo incubator to keep premature babies warm and safe in areas without electricity.
The 1987 Philippine Constitution guarantees every citizen the right to a balanced and healthful ecology in harmony with nature.
The Filipino value of bayanihan encourages communities to clean drainage canals together to prevent mosquito breeding and stop dengue.
The Ifugao people built stone-walled rice terraces that prevent soil erosion and protect mountain communities from dangerous landslides.
During his exile in Dapitan, Jose Rizal built a safe water drainage system to prevent malaria and other diseases.
Barangay health workers act as the local government's first responders by providing free basic medicines and vaccines to children.
Protecting the Philippine Eagle, our national bird, maintains a healthy forest ecosystem that provides clean air and safe water.
Eating traditional Filipino root crops like camote and gabi provides children with healthy fiber and essential vitamins for growth.
Obeying local traffic rules and wearing helmets is a civic duty that keeps Filipino children safe on the road.
Using natural dyes for festival costumes protects participants from harmful skin rashes and dangerous chemical inhalation.
Knowing local Philippine languages helps emergency responders communicate vital health and safety instructions quickly during natural disasters.
The Ivatan people of Batanes build thick limestone houses with cogon roofs to safely withstand strong typhoon winds.
